lessons.title: Modelling Numbers Beyond One Billion

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding and the use of place value for expressing quantities recorded as base ten numerals as well as rounding these to given decimal places and significant figures.

indicator.text: Model number quantities more than 1,000,000,000 using graph sheets, isometric papers and multi-base blocks.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners model and read whole numbers greater than one billion using multi-base blocks, graph sheets and place-value charts.

lessons.title: Comparing and Ordering Huge Numbers

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding and the use of place value for expressing quantities recorded as base ten numerals as well as rounding these to given decimal places and significant figures.

indicator.text: Compare and order whole numbers more than 1,000,000,000 and represent the comparison using “>, <, or =”.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners compare and order whole numbers greater than one billion and record the comparison using >, < or =.

lessons.title: Rounding Whole Numbers

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding and the use of place value for expressing quantities recorded as base ten numerals as well as rounding these to given decimal places and significant figures.

indicator.text: Round (off, up, down) whole numbers more than 1,000,000,000 to the nearest hundred-thousand, ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds and tens.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners round whole numbers greater than one billion to the nearest ten, hundred, thousand, ten-thousand and hundred-thousand.

lessons.title: Rounding Decimals

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding and the use of place value for expressing quantities recorded as base ten numerals as well as rounding these to given decimal places and significant figures.

indicator.text: Round decimals to the nearest tenth, hundredth, thousandths, etc.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners round decimal numbers to the nearest tenth, hundredth and thousandth.

lessons.title: Decimal Places and Significant Figures

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding and the use of place value for expressing quantities recorded as base ten numerals as well as rounding these to given decimal places and significant figures.

indicator.text: Express decimal numerals to given significant and decimal places.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners express decimal numbers to a given number of decimal places and to a given number of significant figures.

lessons.title: Multiplying and Dividing by Powers of Ten

contentStandard.text: Apply mental mathematics strategies and number properties used to solve problems.

indicator.text: Multiply and divide given numbers by powers of 10 including decimals and benchmark fractions.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners multiply and divide whole numbers, decimals and benchmark fractions by 10, 100, 1000 and other powers of ten.

lessons.title: Mental Mathematics Strategies

contentStandard.text: Apply mental mathematics strategies and number properties used to solve problems.

indicator.text: Apply mental mathematics strategies and number properties used to perform calculations.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners apply mental mathematics strategies and number properties to perform calculations without written methods.

lessons.title: Mental Strategies for Word Problems

contentStandard.text: Apply mental mathematics strategies and number properties used to solve problems.

indicator.text: Apply mental mathematics strategies to solve word problems.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners apply mental mathematics strategies to solve word problems.

lessons.title: Adding and Subtracting Four-Digit Numbers

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate an understanding of addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of (i) whole numbers, and (ii) decimal numbers, to solve problems.

indicator.text: Add and subtract up to four-digit numbers.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners add and subtract numbers up to four digits, including decimals, using partitioning and place value.

lessons.title: Multiplying and Dividing Multi-Digit Numbers

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate an understanding of addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of (i) whole numbers, and (ii) decimal numbers, to solve problems.

indicator.text: Multiply or divide multi-digit numbers by 1- and 2-digit numbers.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners multiply and divide multi-digit numbers by one- and two-digit numbers using partitioning, place value and the distributive property.

lessons.title: Story Problems with Decimals

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate an understanding of addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of (i) whole numbers, and (ii) decimal numbers, to solve problems.

indicator.text: Create and solve story problems involving decimals on the four basic operations.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners create and solve story problems involving decimals using all four operations.

lessons.title: Repeated Factors — The Idea of Powers

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding and the use of powers of natural numbers in solving problems.

indicator.text: Illustrate with examples the meaning of repeated factors using counting objects such as bottle tops or bundle sticks.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners illustrate the meaning of repeated factors using concrete objects and write the shorthand index form.

lessons.title: Writing Numbers as Products and Powers

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding and the use of powers of natural numbers in solving problems.

indicator.text: Express a given number as a product of a given number or numbers, as well as, in the form of a power or two such numbers as product of powers.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners express a number as a product of factors, and write that product in index form including as a product of powers.

lessons.title: The Zero Index

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding and the use of powers of natural numbers in solving problems.

indicator.text: Show that the value of any natural number with zero as its exponent or index is 1 and use it to solve problems.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners show that any natural number raised to the power zero equals 1, and use this to solve problems.

lessons.title: Evaluating Numbers in Index Form

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding and the use of powers of natural numbers in solving problems.

indicator.text: Find the value of a number written in index form.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners find the value of a number written in index form, including products of powers and zero indices.

lessons.title: Prime Factors and the Highest Common Factor

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding and the use of powers of natural numbers in solving problems.

indicator.text: Apply the concept of powers of numbers (product of prime) to find Highest Common Factor (HCF).

lessons.learningGoal: Learners use prime factorisation to find the Highest Common Factor of two or more numbers.

lessons.title: Benchmark Fractions, Decimals and Percentages

contentStandard.text: Simplify, compare and order a mixture of positive fractions (i.e. common, percent and decimal) by changing all to equivalent (i) fractions, (ii) decimals, or (iii) percentages.

indicator.text: Determine and recall the percentages and decimals of given benchmark fractions (i.e. tenths, fifths, fourths, thirds and halves) and use these to compare quantities.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners recall the decimal and percentage equivalents of benchmark fractions and use them to compare quantities.

lessons.title: Comparing and Ordering Fractions

contentStandard.text: Simplify, compare and order a mixture of positive fractions (i.e. common, percent and decimal) by changing all to equivalent (i) fractions, (ii) decimals, or (iii) percentages.

indicator.text: Compare and order fractions (i.e. common, percent and decimal fractions up to thousandths) limit to the benchmark fractions.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners compare and order common, decimal and percentage fractions, limited to the benchmarks, by converting them all to the same form.

lessons.title: Adding and Subtracting Unlike and Mixed Fractions

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate an understanding of the process of addition and/or subtraction of fractions and apply this in solving problems.

indicator.text: Explain the process of addition and subtraction of two or three unlike and mixed fractions.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners explain and carry out addition and subtraction of two or three unlike and mixed fractions.

lessons.title: Solving Problems with Fraction Addition and Subtraction

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate an understanding of the process of addition and/or subtraction of fractions and apply this in solving problems.

indicator.text: Solve problems involving addition or subtraction of fractions.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners solve word problems involving the addition and subtraction of fractions.

lessons.title: Multiplying Fractions

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate an understanding of the process of multiplying and dividing positive fractions and apply this in solving problems.

indicator.text: Explain the process of multiplying a fraction (i.e. common, percent and decimal fractions up to thousandths) by a whole number and by a fraction.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners explain and carry out multiplication of a fraction by a whole number and by another fraction.

lessons.title: Finding a Fraction of a Quantity

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate an understanding of the process of multiplying and dividing positive fractions and apply this in solving problems.

indicator.text: Find a fraction of given quantity (i.e. money or given quantity of objects).

lessons.learningGoal: Learners find a fraction of a given quantity of money or objects.

lessons.title: Dividing Fractions

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate an understanding of the process of multiplying and dividing positive fractions and apply this in solving problems.

indicator.text: Explain the process of dividing a fraction (i.e. common, percent and decimal fractions up to thousandths) by a 1-digit whole number and by a fraction.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners explain and carry out division of a fraction by a one-digit whole number and by another fraction.

lessons.title: Dividing Quantities and Fractions by Fractions

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate an understanding of the process of multiplying and dividing positive fractions and apply this in solving problems.

indicator.text: Determine the result of dividing a quantity (i.e. money or objects) or a fraction by a fraction.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners determine the result of dividing a quantity of money or objects, or a fraction, by a fraction.

lessons.title: States of Matter — Sorting the Material World

contentStandard.text: Recognize materials as important resources for providing human needs.

indicator.text: Classify materials into liquids, solids and gases.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can group materials in the environment into liquids, solids and gases.

lessons.title: Why Liquids Matter — Water, Oil, Blood and Sap

contentStandard.text: Recognize materials as important resources for providing human needs.

indicator.text: Discuss the importance of liquids in the life of humans.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can explain why liquids are essential to human life and identify liquids used in their community.

lessons.title: Solids That Keep Us Alive — And Why We Must Preserve Them

contentStandard.text: Recognize materials as important resources for providing human needs.

indicator.text: Discuss the importance of specific solids to life.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can identify solids in the environment that support the survival of humans and other life forms.

lessons.title: The Periodic Table — Twenty Elements in Their Place

contentStandard.text: Understand the periodic table as different elements made up of metals and non-metals and noble gases arranged in an order.

indicator.text: Demonstrate the knowledge of the orderly arrangement of metals, non-metals and noble gases in the periodic table.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can identify the first twenty elements in the periodic table and say which are metals, non-metals and noble gases.

lessons.title: Inside an Animal Cell

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding of the structure of organisms and functions of cells in living systems.

indicator.text: Describe the structure and function of living cells of an animal.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can identify, draw and label an animal cell and state the function of each organelle.

lessons.title: Inside a Plant Cell, and How the Two Differ

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding of the structure of organisms and functions of cells in living systems.

indicator.text: State the functions of each organelle in a plant cell.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can identify, draw, label and model a plant cell, state the function of each organelle, and compare it with an animal cell.

lessons.title: The Inner Planets — Four Worlds Close to the Sun

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate knowledge of the inner planets of the solar system and understand their movement in the system.

indicator.text: Identify the inner planets of the solar system and describe their properties.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can identify the inner planets of the solar system and describe their properties.

lessons.title: Building the Solar System — The Model Task

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate knowledge of the inner planets of the solar system and understand their movement in the system.

indicator.text: Identify the inner planets of the solar system and describe their properties.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can design and construct a model of the solar system and explain what it shows.

lessons.title: Mercury and Venus — Properties and Relative Motion

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate knowledge of the inner planets of the solar system and understand their movement in the system.

indicator.text: Discuss the properties and the relative motions of the planets Mercury and Venus.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can outline the properties of Mercury and Venus and describe their movement around the Sun.

lessons.title: Day, Night and the Year — Consolidation

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate knowledge of the inner planets of the solar system and understand their movement in the system.

indicator.text: The source indicator concerns Mercury and Venus; alignment to this topic needs review.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can explain day and night and the year in terms of rotation and revolution, and demonstrate their understanding with a model.

review.message: This recap covers Earth's rotation and revolution, but the source indicator addresses Mercury and Venus. Editorial alignment pending.

lessons.title: The Water Cycle — How It Happens

contentStandard.text: Recognise that the water cycle is an example of repeated patterns of change in nature and understand how it occurs.

indicator.text: Explain how the water cycle occurs as a repeated pattern in nature.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can identify the stages of the water cycle, explain how they are linked, and demonstrate the process of transpiration and cloud formation.

lessons.title: Why the Water Cycle Matters

contentStandard.text: Recognise that the water cycle is an example of repeated patterns of change in nature and understand how it occurs.

indicator.text: Describe the importance of the water cycle in nature.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can describe the importance of the water cycle in terms of energy, nutrients, the water table, weather and clean water.

lessons.title: The Life Cycle of the Housefly

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate the skills of carrying out activities to show the stages of the life cycle of a housefly, the effects of its activities on humans and how to reduce them.

indicator.text: Describe the life cycle of the housefly.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can identify and describe the stages of the life cycle of the housefly and arrange them in the correct order.

lessons.title: Rearing and Recording — The Housefly Diary

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate the skills of carrying out activities to show the stages of the life cycle of a housefly, the effects of its activities on humans and how to reduce them.

indicator.text: Describe the life cycle of the housefly.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can observe, record and interpret the stages of the housefly life cycle over time.

lessons.title: The Housefly as a Menace

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate the skills of carrying out activities to show the stages of the life cycle of a housefly, the effects of its activities on humans and how to reduce them.

indicator.text: Discuss the activities of the housefly as a menace to humans and show how to reduce the effects of those activities.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can describe how the housefly's feeding habits and activities affect humans, and identify the diseases it can transfer.

lessons.title: Designing the Intervention — Breaking the Cycle

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate the skills of carrying out activities to show the stages of the life cycle of a housefly, the effects of its activities on humans and how to reduce them.

indicator.text: Discuss the activities of the housefly as a menace to humans and show how to reduce the effects of those activities.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can design an intervention that reduces the effects of the housefly's activities on humans, and educate their community about it.

lessons.title: Plant Nutrient Sources — Organic and Inorganic

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding of the different plant nutrients (organic and inorganic fertilizers) and their application in school farming (school gardening).

indicator.text: Observe and list all plant nutrient sources available in a community and categorise them into organic and inorganic nutrient sources.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can observe and list plant nutrient sources in the community, categorise them as organic or inorganic, and explain the difference.

lessons.title: How Each Nutrient Is Applied in the Field

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding of the different plant nutrients (organic and inorganic fertilizers) and their application in school farming (school gardening).

indicator.text: Describe the physical characteristics of different plant nutrients (organic and inorganic) and how each is applied to plants in the field.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can describe the physical characteristics of organic and inorganic nutrients and how each is applied to plants in the field.

lessons.title: School Garden Practical — Applying What We Learned

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding of the different plant nutrients (organic and inorganic fertilizers) and their application in school farming (school gardening).

indicator.text: Describe the physical characteristics of different plant nutrients (organic and inorganic) and how each is applied to plants in the field.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can demonstrate the practical application of each type of plant nutrient to plants in the field, and run a fair test of their effects.

lessons.title: Cycles in Review — Connections Across Systems
lessons.subStrand: Earth Science; Life Cycle of Organisms; Crop Production

contentStandard.text: Integrates several cycle standards; exact mapping needs editorial review.

indicator.text: Cross-topic recap; exact indicator mapping needs editorial review.

lessons.learningGoal: Compare patterns across the water cycle, housefly life cycle and crop production.

review.message: This lesson combines several cycle topics and source indicators. Exact alignment needs editorial review.

lessons.title: Forms of Energy and How They Are Related

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate an understanding of forms of energy and their daily applications.

indicator.text: Identify the various forms of energy and show how they are related.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can list the forms of energy and demonstrate, with diagrams, how potential energy and kinetic energy are related.

lessons.title: Energy in Daily Life, and Calculating PE and KE

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate an understanding of forms of energy and their daily applications.

indicator.text: Explain daily applications of forms of energy.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can match forms of energy to appliances used at school, at home and in the community, and use PE = mgh and KE = ½mv² to solve simple problems.

lessons.title: Light — Straight Lines, Reflection and Refraction

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding of characteristics of light, such as travelling in a straight line, reflection, refraction and dispersion.

indicator.text: Demonstrate how light travels in a straight line.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can perform experiments showing that light travels in a straight line and can be reflected and refracted, and produce reports, posters or diagrams.

lessons.title: Dispersion — Splitting White Light

contentStandard.text: Demonstrate understanding of characteristics of light, such as travelling in a straight line, reflection, refraction and dispersion.

indicator.text: The source indicator concerns straight-line light travel; alignment to dispersion needs review.

lessons.learningGoal: Learners can perform an experiment to show the dispersion of light into colours, and report on all four characteristics of light studied this term.

review.message: The lesson covers dispersion, while its source indicator names straight-line light travel. Editorial alignment pending.
